issues.legal_issue: A sufficiently explained delay in filing a review petition may be condoned.
material_facts: The review petition was filed 320 days late.
The materials submitted showed that steps had been taken at various levels within the Ministry.
issues.conclusion: The Court accepted the explanation and condoned the delay.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered whether sufficient cause had been shown for the delay and accepted the explanation supported by the application for condonation.

predicates.review_proceeding: A party has filed a petition asking the court to review its earlier judgment.
predicates.delay_in_filing: The review petition was filed after the applicable filing period.
predicates.explanation_shows_steps_taken_to_file: The explanation for the delay describes steps taken within the petitioning institution to prepare and file the petition.

issues.definition: When a review petition is late and the explanation describes steps taken to file it, the delay is condoned.

issues.legal_issue: A clerical misquotation in a judgment may be corrected in review by deleting the material that was wrongly attributed to a source.
material_facts: The earlier judgment attributed four lines to an expert committee report that were not part of that report.
The Court found that the added lines resulted from a clerical mistake.
issues.conclusion: The Court deleted the misquoted lines and the corresponding portion of the earlier judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Constitution, Order XL Rule 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1966, and Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 permit review on specified grounds, including an apparent mistake or error on the face of the record.

predicates.review_proceeding: A party has filed a petition asking the court to review its earlier judgment.
predicates.source_misquoted_through_clerical_mistak: The earlier judgment attributed material to a source that was not in that source because of a clerical mistake.

issues.definition: In a review proceeding, material wrongly attributed to a source through a clerical mistake is deleted.

issues.legal_issue: A misquotation that can be removed without undermining the remaining reasoning does not make the earlier judgment erroneous as a whole.
material_facts: The earlier judgment relied in part on an expert committee report containing lines that had been misquoted.
The Court concluded that the judgment remained reasoned even after those lines were removed.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the misquotation did not make the earlier judgment erroneous on the face of the law and that the judgment stood on its remaining reasoning.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 137 of the Constitution, Order XL Rule 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1966, and Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, review addresses specified errors; correction of a discrete mistake does not require disturbing reasoning that remains supported without it.

predicates.review_proceeding: A party has filed a petition asking the court to review its earlier judgment.
predicates.misquoted_material_is_severable: The material wrongly attributed to a source can be removed from the earlier judgment as a distinct portion.
predicates.remaining_reasoning_stands_without_it: The reasoning in the earlier judgment remains supported after the wrongly attributed material is removed.

issues.definition: If wrongly attributed material can be removed and the remaining reasoning still stands, the underlying reasoning remains supported.

issues.legal_issue: Review jurisdiction does not permit a party to obtain reconsideration merely because another interpretation of an issue already decided is possible.
material_facts: The review petitioner disputed the earlier interpretation of statutory provisions governing applications for mining leases.
The earlier judgment had already considered and answered that interpretive issue.
The review petitioner advanced an alternative view rather than identifying an apparent error or a grave mistake.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected this ground for review.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Constitution, Order XL Rule 1 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1966, and Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 confine review to specified grounds. In Chhajju Ram v. Neki and Moran Mar Basselios Catholicos v. Most Rev. Mar Poulose Athanasius, “any other sufficient reason” was understood as a reason analogous to the stated grounds. Parsion Devi v. Sumitri Devi holds that review is not an appeal in disguise, that an error requiring reasoning to detect is not apparent on the face of the record, and that an erroneous decision cannot simply be reheard and corrected.

rule.if: review_proceeding and issue_already_decided and alternative_interpretation_asserted and no_apparent_or_patent_error

predicates.review_proceeding: A party has filed a petition asking the court to review its earlier judgment.
predicates.issue_already_decided: The earlier judgment considered and answered the issue raised again.
predicates.alternative_interpretation_asserted: The petitioner contends that the issue should be resolved according to a different interpretation.
predicates.no_apparent_or_patent_error: The petitioner has not shown an error apparent on the record, a patent mistake, or a grave error in the earlier judgment.

issues.definition: A different interpretation of an issue already decided does not justify review when no apparent or patent error is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A past governmental commitment cannot displace the governing statutory criteria for deciding mining-lease applications after an area has been notified for re-grant.
material_facts: A State Government had allegedly committed to grant mining leases in the future in connection with a proposed project.
The commitment was invoked years later, after commercial operations at the project had begun.
The area was notified for re-grant and applications were invited from the mining public.
The review petitioner sought to reargue the effect of the commitment, which had already been considered in the earlier judgment.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the applications had to be decided under the governing Act and rules, and that the State Government could not grant a lease on the basis of a past commitment in disregard of the statutory criteria.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Sections 2, 11(1), and 11(3) of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, and the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960. It held that the State Government acts as a statutory delegate, cannot act inconsistently with the Act, and has no authority under that framework to promise a future mining lease in return for investment. Once an area is notified for re-grant, applications must be decided under the Act and rules rather than on the basis of such a commitment.

rule.if: review_proceeding and area_notified_for_regrant and prior_commitment_invoked and competing_applications_require_decision

predicates.review_proceeding: A party has filed a petition asking the court to review its earlier judgment.
predicates.area_notified_for_regrant: The government has made an area available again for grant and invited applications for it.
predicates.prior_commitment_invoked: An applicant relies on a government promise made earlier to obtain a lease.
predicates.competing_applications_require_decision: Applications from multiple applicants must be considered for the lease.

issues.definition: Where an area is notified for re-grant and competing applications are to be decided, an earlier government commitment invoked by an applicant does not replace the governing legal criteria.

issues.legal_issue: A State Government cannot frame or apply a mineral policy contrary to the governing statutory framework.
material_facts: The review petitioner raised an issue about mineral policies.
The earlier judgment had already considered the State's authority to frame policy outside the governing Act and rules.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the contention, holding that the State could not frame a policy outside the Act and rules.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the parliamentary declaration and the governing Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 and Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, as discussed in the earlier judgment and in the decisions referred to there.

predicates.review_proceeding: A party has filed a petition asking the court to review its earlier judgment.
predicates.state_policy_conflicts_with_statutory_fr: A State Government policy would operate contrary to the legal framework governing the subject.

issues.definition: In a review proceeding, a State Government policy that conflicts with the governing statutory framework cannot override that framework.
